label: CLAIM LEDGER
note: Every entry is re-measured on every run. A drifting residual is a finding, not a warning. The counts describe ONE committed claims file read by an exit-code contract -- they are not a score of how good an agent's work is, and nothing here survives the day a run supplies its own claims file. The corpus is fixed precisely so that a change here means the instrument moved, not that some run got more honest.

instrument.note: Editing this file is itself a measurable event, and the pin is re-derived by scripts/check_traps.py rather than by the file being pinned -- an edited copy of the instrument would report that it is fine. The harness reports both hashes and never resolves to a passing verdict on a modified instrument.

claims_pin.note: The file under judgement is pinned as well as the instrument. Without this the ledger would keep re-proving the previous change's claims forever, and the gate would read PASS on a measurement about something else. Applied mode -- a run's own claims file -- therefore reports claims_are_the_pinned_ones false and its verdict FAIL by construction, which is the correct answer and not a defect.

facts.claim: the claims file being judged is the one this ledger pinned
facts.origin: measured; a ledger pinning the previous change re-proves the previous change's claims forever

facts.claim: the instrument that produced this measurement is the one this ledger pinned
facts.origin: measured; the correlated-instrument failure is only catchable if the instrument is pinned

facts.claim: the claims file was not authored by the run under judgement
facts.origin: measured; a run that writes the claims it asks to be judged by writes the questions too

facts.claim: every claim in the pinned corpus was reproduced by the check it names
the pinned corpus holds this many claims
every claim in the corpus names a check that can be run
facts.origin: measured; a claim with no check is indistinguishable from a passing one in a verdict-only report

facts.claim: both claims were reproduced by running the check they name
facts.origin: measured; the second is the exact negation of the refuted claim in contradicted.json, over the same scope

facts.claim: no claim in the corpus is refuted by the check it names
facts.origin: measured; the failure this skill exists for, and the corpus that must be able to produce it is fixtures/claims/contradicted.json

facts.claim: no claim is reported as verified without a check to run
no claim is evidenced by a command that exits 0 without examining anything
facts.origin: measured; `true` verifies every claim in the world and nothing in particular

facts.claim: every check references the scope its claim names
facts.origin: measured as a string test, which is weaker than the sentence sounds; references/limits.md

facts.claim: no named check failed to execute
facts.origin: measured; a check that cannot run is a result, not an exception

facts.claim: the measurement imports no model and no network module
facts.origin: re-derived every run from this file's own AST rather than asserted as a constant, and re-derived a second time by check_traps.py

unbound: no claim here is about the quality of the work. A claim can be true, reproduced, and worthless, and this gate cannot tell those apart -- it says the outcome was reproduced, not that it was worth reproducing.
these counts describe two claims. They are not a rate, a distribution, or a population, and no claim about agents in general may be read off them.

a check that references the scope its claim names is in scope. That is a string test, not a proof the check establishes the claim: references/limits.md records a fixture that passed it while asserting something unrelated.
the verdict is scoped to exit codes. Whether a check would have FAILED had the world been different is a property of the check, and nothing in this ledger re-derives it.
